integrated_description: The default pathway is adoption-first — prioritizing breed-specific rescues and including adult and senior animals — with a clearly defined exception process permitting purchase from a rigorously vetted breeder (requiring health testing, full transparency, welfare standards, return clauses, and no broker sales) only after documented good-faith adoption searching has failed to meet specific welfare or functional needs (e.g., service animal roles). All adopters must complete a pre-placement compatibility assessment and commit to a measurable surrender-risk reduction plan covering housing stability, training capacity, a veterinary budget, and contingency plans for medical or behavioral challenges, supplemented by a defined post-adoption follow-up window with rescue or shelter support. The systemic commitment extends beyond the individual placement through at least one tangible ongoing contribution — such as shelter volunteering, fostering, financial support, or participation in low-cost spay/neuter and community education initiatives — framed explicitly around supporting adoption and responsible long-term pet retention rather than reinforcing a simplistic adopt-vs-buy binary.
integration_rationale: All three stakeholders accepted the core foster-to-adopt synthesis and their modifications were largely complementary — stakeholder_a's adoption-first default with breeder exception criteria, stakeholder_b's post-adoption surrender-risk and systemic support requirements, and stakeholder_c's operational measurability and advocacy reframing — allowing full integration without substantive conflict by layering each modification as a distinct operational tier within the same process-centered framework.
